title: SLO Lease Rebalancer for Soft Regional Handoffs
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce SLO Lease Rebalancer: enables controlled handoff of SLO responsibility between regions with time-boxed soft resume and capacity-aware lease migration. Config knobs: lease_window_ms, handoff_threshold_pct, emergency_force_reclaim. No user-facing API changes.
description: Background: Regional incidents and maintenance windows frequently force temporary redistribution of SLO responsibility across regions. Existing failover semantics are abrupt: either route fully to a fallback region or trigger a global throttle, which causes avoidable churn and user-visible latency spikes. This PR implements a SLO Lease Rebalancer that permits soft, capacity-aware handoffs: regions can donate or acquire SLO leases over a bounded window, with attenuated traffic shifts, circuit-aware backoff, and an emergency reclaim path for correctness. Design highlights: 1) Lease model: each region holds leases for tenant partitions with a lease_window_ms TTL and an associated capacity_score updated from per-route throughput and node health. 2) Rebalancer algorithm: periodic scoring pass computes donors and receivers and proposes chunked lease transfers sized by capacity_delta and handoff_threshold_pct. Transfers are staged over windows with exponential backoff on transient failures. 3) Soft resume: receivers apply an attenuated activation that gradually increases weight (0 -> target) so downstream caches and KV warmup reduce cold-start SLO violations. 4) Circuit interplay: when a receiving region has active circuits tripped for a tenant, the transfer is paused and marked for retry; donors maintain temporary sticky leases until a safe handoff can complete. 5) Observability: new lease_migration_success/failure, lease_transfer_duration_ms, and region_capacity_score metrics plus handoff traces. 6) Safety: emergency_force_reclaim shortcut (operator-triggered) for edge cases and a conservatively defaulted handoff_threshold_pct=0.25 to avoid aggressive churn. Changes made: - runtime/lease_manager.go: core rebalancer, scoring, transfer orchestration, retry/backoff. - runtime/lease_manager_test.go: unit tests covering scoring, chunking, backoff semantics. - routing/handshake.go: handshake extension for staged weight updates and compatibility checks. - observability/metrics/lease_metrics.prom: metric definitions and dashboard hints. - docs/operational/lease-rebalancer.md: runbook, default knobs, and troubleshooting. - deploy/k8s/upgrade-hooks.yaml: prestop hook to drain leases on node removal. - cli/ctl-handoff.sh: convenience operator script to trigger handoffs or force-reclaim. - ops/runbooks/slo-hand-offs.md: incident runbook additions. - examples/handshake-sim.json: simulation scenarios used in testing. Testing and validation: comprehensive unit coverage added; integration test in perf-canary simulated a cross-region outage and validated a staged handoff with 0.12% SLO breach delta (within target). Chaos testing included region-level partitioning and node terminations; rebalancer paused transfers and resumed once capacity stabilized. Performance: small CPU overhead (~3% p99 increase during active rebalances) observed in canary, within SLA. Rollout plan: canary at 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 2h, monitor lease_migration_success, slo_violation_rate, region_capacity_score and downstream error/latency. If stable, ramp to 25% for 4h then global. Auto rollback on >0.5% sustained increase in SLO breaches for 15m or >2s median token latency regression. Backwards compatibility: no changes to public APIs; all behavior behind runtime feature-flag runtime.slo_lease_rebalancer.enabled=false by default for safe staged rollout. Operator knobs: lease_window_ms (default 900000), handoff_threshold_pct (default 0.25), max_chunk_size (default 100 partitions), emergency_force_reclaim (manual). Migration and upgrade notes: ensure dedicated nodes have upgrade-hooks applied to allow graceful lease drain; upgrade order should follow cross-region canary then control plane. Known limitations and mitigations: in extreme multi-region partition churn the rebalancer defers transfers to avoid oscillation; we log deferred_transfer_* metrics to aid future tuning. Documentation added and internal runbooks updated. Checklist: [x] Implementation and tests, [x] Integration/perf canary, [x] Observability and runbooks, [x] Operator scripts, [x] Reviewed and approved. This description consolidates rationale, design, testing, and rollout guidance for operators and reviewers.

review_conversation: Ethan Patel: Can you explain how this avoids oscillation when two regions try to rebalance simultaneously? Reply: The scoring pass is leader-elected per-tenant-partition and uses monotonic timestamps plus a proposed-token based compare to avoid split decisions; we also add a jittered backoff on retries.

Riley Gonzales: Request: add metric for deferred_transfer_count and a debug flag to force single-step transfers. Reply: Added deferred_transfer_count and ctl-handoff now supports --force-single-step for operator testing.

Samira Noor: Question about SLA impact on hot path: why not warm cache before weight increase? Reply: soft resume increments weight in 10% steps with 30s spacing by default; this was tuned in canary to balance warmup vs failover speed.
Ethan Patel: Approve after addressing lint and adding runbook section on emergency_force_reclaim. Reply: Lint fixed and runbook extended.
Riley Gonzales: Approved on green CI.

rollout_plan: Canary 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 2 hours, monitor lease_migration_success and slo_violation_rate; if stable ramp to 25% for 4 hours then global. Auto rollback on >0.5% sustained SLO breach increase for 15m.
rollback_plan: Feature-flag flip to disable runtime.slo_lease_rebalancer.enabled=false instantly disables rebalancer; operator script ctl-handoff.sh --reclaim can force donor sticky leases back. In case of systemic regressions, revert the commit on main and trigger emergency reclaim per runbook.
testing_summary: Unit tests exercise scoring and backoff; integration tests simulate cross-region outage; perf-canary measured p50/p95/p99 token latency and CPU; chaos engineering (region partition) validated pause/resume semantics. Synthetic traffic sim harness included in examples/handshake-sim.json.
motivation: Provide a less disruptive, observability-first approach for moving SLO responsibility across regions so we can perform maintenance and partial failovers without large user-visible regressions.
